title: DYNAMITE: A high-performance framework for solving Dynamical Mean-Field Equations
summary:
Understanding the dynamics of systems evolving in complex and rugged energy landscapes is central across physics, economics, biology, and computer science. Disordered mean-field models provide a powerful framework, as exact Dynamical Mean-Field Equations (DMFE) can be derived. However, solving the DMFE -- a set of coupled integral-differential equations for two-time functions -- remains a major numerical challenge.
  So far, large-time solutions of DMFE rely either on analytical approaches, such as the Cugliandolo--Kurchan ansatz based on assumptions like weak ergodicity breaking (which is known to fail in some cases), or on numerical integrations that reliably reach times $O(10^3)$ and extend further only via poorly controlled approximations. Consequently, no general method currently exists to solve DMFE at very long times, limiting the study of slow dynamics in complex landscapes.
  We present \textsc{Dynamite} (DYNAmical Mean-fIeld Time Evolution solver), a high-performance framework for solving DMFE up to unprecedented times $t=O(10^7)$. It combines non-uniform interpolation, adaptive time stepping, and numerical `renormalization' of memory, enabling accurate evaluation of history integrals. Its asymptotic runtime is linear, with sublinear memory scaling. Stability and precision are ensured via an adaptive Runge--Kutta scheme and periodic sparsification of the past.
  \textsc{Dynamite} achieves orders-of-magnitude speedups over uniform-grid methods while maintaining accuracy and reproducibility on CPU and GPU architectures. Benchmarks on glassy mean-field models, including the mixed spherical $p$-spin system, demonstrate access to aging and relaxation regimes previously out of reach. The framework provides a reproducible and extensible foundation for studying long-memory dynamical systems.

AI.tldr: Dynamite is a high-performance framework for solving Dynamical Mean-Field Equations up to unprecedented times t=O(10^7) using non-uniform interpolation, adaptive time stepping, and memory renormalization, enabling study of slow dynamics in complex landscapes.
AI.motivation: Current methods for solving Dynamical Mean-Field Equations (DMFE) are limited: analytical approaches rely on assumptions like weak ergodicity breaking that can fail, while numerical methods only reach times O(10^3) with poorly controlled approximations for longer times. This prevents study of slow dynamics in complex energy landscapes across physics, economics, biology, and computer science.
AI.method: Dynamite combines non-uniform interpolation, adaptive time stepping, and numerical 'renormalization' of memory to accurately evaluate history integrals. It uses an adaptive Runge-Kutta scheme for stability and precision, with periodic sparsification of past data. The framework achieves linear asymptotic runtime with sublinear memory scaling.
AI.result: Dynamite achieves orders-of-magnitude speedups over uniform-grid methods while maintaining accuracy and reproducibility on both CPU and GPU architectures. Benchmarks on glassy mean-field models, including the mixed spherical p-spin system, demonstrate access to aging and relaxation regimes previously out of reach.
AI.conclusion: Dynamite provides a reproducible and extensible foundation for studying long-memory dynamical systems, enabling solution of DMFE up to unprecedented times t=O(10^7) and overcoming previous limitations in studying slow dynamics in complex landscapes.

title: Disorder averaging in random lattice models with periodic boundary conditions: Application to models with uncorrelated and correlated disorder
summary: Periodic boundary conditions are not always used in the study of disordered systems, but it can be advantageous to apply them to mimick thermodynamically large systems. In this case, polarization and its cumulants can not be obtained directly, but through the tools of the modern theory of polarization. This theory casts the polarization in crystalline systems as a geometric phase, rather than an operator expectation value. We develop disorder averaging techniques within the context of this theory which can calculate the variance of the polarization, its higher order moments, and the excess kurtosis (or Binder cumulant). We also derive an indicator of delocalization based on the degeneracy as a function of boundary conditions. We apply the computational techniques to two model systems. To test localization, we use a one-dimensional disordered model which is fully Anderson localized. Our calculations verify this. We also apply our techniques to the one dimensional de Moura-Lyra model, developed to study power law correlated (controlled by a parameter, $α$) disorder. While this model is a pathological one, our method is validated. We also point out the significance of pairwise degeneracies found in the parameter range, $α>2$ and near the band center (or near half filling), where the model was conjectured to exhibit a mobility edge.

AI.tldr: Developed disorder averaging techniques within modern polarization theory to calculate polarization variance, higher moments, and excess kurtosis for disordered systems with periodic boundary conditions, with applications to Anderson localization and power-law correlated disorder models.
AI.motivation: Periodic boundary conditions are useful for mimicking thermodynamically large systems in disordered systems, but polarization and its cumulants cannot be obtained directly. The modern theory of polarization provides a framework for treating polarization as a geometric phase rather than an operator expectation value, but techniques for disorder averaging within this context need development.
AI.method: Developed disorder averaging techniques within the modern theory of polarization framework to calculate polarization variance, higher order moments, and excess kurtosis (Binder cumulant). Also derived a delocalization indicator based on degeneracy as a function of boundary conditions. Applied computational techniques to two model systems: (1) a 1D disordered model with full Anderson localization, and (2) the 1D de Moura-Lyra model with power-law correlated disorder controlled by parameter α.
AI.result: For the fully Anderson localized 1D model, calculations verified the expected localization behavior. For the de Moura-Lyra model, the method was validated despite the model's pathological nature. Pairwise degeneracies were observed in the parameter range α>2 near the band center (half filling), where the model was conjectured to exhibit a mobility edge.
AI.conclusion: Successfully developed and validated disorder averaging techniques within modern polarization theory for studying disordered systems with periodic boundary conditions. The methods enable calculation of polarization statistics and provide indicators for localization properties, with applications to both conventional Anderson localization and models with power-law correlated disorder.

title: Projector, Neural, and Tensor-Network Representations of $\mathbb{Z}_N$ Cluster and Dipolar-cluster SPT States
summary: The $\mathbb{Z}_N$ cluster-state wavefunction, a paradigmatic example of symmetry-protected topological (SPT) order with $\mathbb{Z}_N \times \mathbb{Z}_N$ symmetry, is expressed in various equivalent ways. We identify the projector-based scheme called the $P$-representation as the efficient way to express cluster and dipolar cluster state's wavefunctions. Employing the restricted Boltzmann machine scheme to re-write the interaction matrix in the $P$-representation in terms of neural weight matrices allows us to develop the neural quantum state (NQS) and the matrix product state (MPS) representations of the same state. The NQS and MPS representations differ only in the way the weight matrices are split and grouped together in a matrix product. For both $\mathbb{Z}_N$ cluster and dipolar cluster states, we derive in closed form the weight function $W(s,h)$ that couples physical spins $s$ to hidden variables $h$, generalizing the previous construction for $Z_2$ cluster states to $\mathbb{Z}_N$. For the dipolar cluster state protected by two charge and two dipole symmetries, the procedure we have developed leads to the tensor product state (TPS) representation of the wavefunction where each local tensor carries three virtual indices connecting a given site to two nearest neighbors and one further neighbor. We benchmark the resulting TPS construction against conventional MPS representation using density-matrix renormalization group simulations and argue that the TPS could offer a more efficient representation for some modulated SPT states. As a by-product of the investigation, we generalize the previous $Z_2$ matrix product operator construction of the Kramers-Wannier (KW) operator to $\mathbb{Z}_N$ and interprets it as the dipolar generalization of the discrete Fourier transform on $\mathbb{Z}_N$ variables. The new interpretation naturally explains why the KW map is non-invertible.

AI.tldr: The paper develops efficient representations (NQS, MPS, TPS) for ℤₙ cluster and dipolar cluster states using P-representation and neural weight matrices, generalizing from ℤ₂ to ℤₙ, and interprets the Kramers-Wannier operator as a dipolar Fourier transform.
AI.motivation: To develop efficient representations for ℤₙ cluster and dipolar cluster states (SPT phases) that generalize previous ℤ₂ constructions, and to provide new interpretations of mathematical structures like the Kramers-Wannier operator.
AI.method: Uses P-representation (projector-based scheme) to express cluster states, then employs restricted Boltzmann machine scheme to rewrite interaction matrices as neural weight matrices, enabling derivation of NQS and MPS representations. For dipolar cluster states, develops TPS representation with local tensors carrying three virtual indices.
AI.result: Derived closed-form weight function W(s,h) for ℤₙ cluster and dipolar cluster states, generalized ℤ₂ matrix product operator construction of Kramers-Wannier operator to ℤₙ, and showed TPS can be more efficient than conventional MPS for modulated SPT states based on DMRG benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: The P-representation provides an efficient framework for representing cluster states, enabling unified NQS/MPS/TPS constructions that generalize to ℤₙ symmetries. The Kramers-Wannier operator is interpreted as a dipolar Fourier transform, explaining its non-invertibility. TPS representations may offer advantages for certain modulated SPT states.

title: Accelerating Quantum State Encoding with SIMD: Design, Implementation, and Benchmarking
comment: Published in: 2025 9th International Conference On Electrical, Electronics And Information Engineering (ICEEIE)
summary: Efficient data encoding is the main factor affecting how fast hybrid quantum-classical algorithms run, but traditional simulators spend most of their time changing classical features into quantum rotations. This work introduces Hybriqu Encoder, a Rust-based, SIMD-aware kernel that focuses exclusively on angle encoding and integrates transparently with Python via CFFI. The kernel processes four double-precision rotations at once using AVX-class vector lanes, combines data in a way that fits well with the cache and uses pre-calculated trigonometric factors, while keeping all unsafe operations within a safe Rust interface. Benchmarks on Apple Silicon show that using pure angle encoding is 5.4% faster at 64 qubits, and the speedup increases as the amount of data exceeds the L1 cache size, while kernels that quickly apply rotations to the entire state vector are limited by memory and do not benefit from SIMD. These results indicate that using vectorization leads to consistent improvements when calculations are the main focus, but limits on data transfer speed prevent additional speed increases, highlighting the need for future efforts on better state updates and choosing between different processing methods. By combining smart optimization that considers the architecture with Rust's safety features, the Hybriqu Encoder offers a flexible base for bigger, mixed systems designed to reduce data encoding delays in future hybrid quantum-classical processes.

AI.tldr: Hybriqu Encoder is a Rust-based SIMD-optimized kernel for angle encoding in quantum simulations that achieves 5.4% speedup at 64 qubits through AVX vectorization and cache-aware data processing.
AI.motivation: Traditional quantum simulators spend excessive time converting classical features to quantum rotations, creating a bottleneck in hybrid quantum-classical algorithms where efficient data encoding is critical for performance.
AI.method: Developed a Rust-based SIMD-aware kernel using AVX vector lanes to process four double-precision rotations simultaneously, implemented cache-aware data layout, pre-calculated trigonometric factors, and exposed unsafe operations through a safe Rust interface with Python integration via CFFI.
AI.result: Achieved 5.4% speedup at 64 qubits with pure angle encoding, with speedup increasing as data exceeds L1 cache size; memory-bound kernels applying rotations to entire state vectors didn't benefit from SIMD, showing vectorization only helps when computation is the bottleneck.
AI.conclusion: Vectorization provides consistent improvements for compute-bound operations but is limited by memory bandwidth; future work should focus on better state updates and algorithm selection, with Hybriqu Encoder serving as an architecture-aware, safe foundation for reducing data encoding delays in hybrid quantum-classical systems.

title: Optimization of entanglement harvesting with arbitrary temporal profiles: the limit of second order perturbation theory
summary: We study the protocol of entanglement harvesting when two local probes couple to the vacuum of a real scalar quantum field with arbitrary temporal profiles. We use a Hermite expansion to efficiently compute smeared field propagators in closed-form, recasting the negativity between the probes as a matrix product. We then optimize the protocol under different signalling conditions, enhancing entanglement harvesting by several orders of magnitude. This optimization would take current experimental proposals beyond the regime of second order perturbation theory.

AI.tldr: Optimized entanglement harvesting protocol using Hermite expansion for efficient computation of smeared field propagators, enabling significant entanglement enhancement beyond perturbation theory limits.
AI.motivation: To improve entanglement harvesting from quantum field vacuum by developing efficient computational methods that can optimize temporal coupling profiles and overcome limitations of second-order perturbation theory.
AI.method: Use Hermite expansion to compute smeared field propagators in closed-form, recast negativity between probes as matrix product, and optimize protocol under different signalling conditions.
AI.result: Achieved entanglement harvesting enhancement by several orders of magnitude, pushing beyond regime of second-order perturbation theory for current experimental proposals.
AI.conclusion: The developed method enables significant optimization of entanglement harvesting protocols, making previously inaccessible regimes experimentally feasible through efficient computational techniques.

title: Heterogeneous architectures enable a 138x reduction in physical qubit requirements for fault-tolerant quantum computing under detailed accounting
summary: Quantum computer hardware is predicted to scale over hundreds of thousands of qubits coming online in the next decade. Despite significant theoretical and experimental QEC progress, quantum computer architecture has suffered a significant gap, with bottom-up physical-device-driven challenges largely disconnected from top-down QEC-code-driven considerations. In this work, we unify these two views, presenting a complete heterogeneous quantum computing architecture incorporating task-specific hardware selection and QEC encoding, and agnostic to code selection or physical qubit parameters. Our approach further enables special-purpose processing modules, and includes a full microarchitecture for fault-tolerant implementation of interfaces between quantum processing units and quantum memories. Using this architecture and a new fully featured compiler functioning across subsystems at the scale of $1,000$ logical qubits, we schedule and orchestrate a variety of algorithms down to hardware-specific instructions; a detailed accounting of all operations reveals up to 551x reduction in algorithmic logical error and up to 138x reduction in physical-qubit overhead compared to a monolithic baseline architecture. We then consider the factorization of 2048-bit RSA-integers; using an experimentally demonstrated grid-coupling topology, factoring RSA-2048 requires 381k physical qubits and 9.2 days, which can be reduced to 4.9 days via addition of an algorithm-specific accelerator for the Adder subroutine (requiring 439k qubits). Finally, assuming hypothetical long-range coupling, implementing quantum memory using qLDPC codes reduces the resources required for factoring to just 190k qubits and under 10 days. These results and the tooling we have built indicate that heterogeneous quantum-computer architectures can deliver significant, verifiable benefits on realistic hardware.

AI.tldr: A heterogeneous quantum computing architecture that bridges physical hardware and QEC considerations, enabling significant reductions in logical error and qubit overhead, with demonstrated benefits for RSA-2048 factoring.
AI.motivation: Address the disconnect between bottom-up physical-device-driven challenges and top-down QEC-code-driven considerations in quantum computer architecture, which has created a significant gap despite progress in quantum error correction.
AI.method: Develop a complete heterogeneous quantum computing architecture incorporating task-specific hardware selection and QEC encoding, agnostic to code selection or physical qubit parameters. Includes a full microarchitecture for fault-tolerant interfaces between quantum processing units and memories, plus a new compiler functioning across subsystems at 1,000 logical qubits scale.
AI.result: Up to 551x reduction in algorithmic logical error and up to 138x reduction in physical-qubit overhead compared to monolithic baseline. For RSA-2048 factoring: 381k physical qubits and 9.2 days with grid-coupling topology; reduced to 4.9 days with adder accelerator (439k qubits); further reduced to 190k qubits and under 10 days using qLDPC codes with hypothetical long-range coupling.
AI.conclusion: Heterogeneous quantum-computer architectures can deliver significant, verifiable benefits on realistic hardware by unifying physical device considerations with QEC requirements, enabling practical large-scale quantum computing with reduced resource overhead.

title: Probing the Planck scale with quantum computation
summary: General relativity and quantum mechanics are incompatible at the Planck scale. This contention can be examined if a quantum computer is set to operate at a rate that exceeds the classical limit of one operation per Planck volume-time, or equivalently $2^{491}$ m$^{-3}$ s$^{-1}$. Here we quantify the relation between the logical qubit count and the extent to which classicality is challenged. We argue that 500 logical qubits are sufficient to reject theories confined to a laboratory. We account for the operational cost of computation and communication at all scales up to and including the observable universe, ultimately constrained by a 1600-logical-qubit computer. Remarkably, current plans for commercial quantum computers are projected to surpass this limit, thereby putting the quantum-gravity standoff to the test.

AI.tldr: 500 logical qubits can challenge classical physics in lab settings; 1600 logical qubits can test quantum-gravity incompatibility across the observable universe; commercial quantum computers may soon reach this threshold.
AI.motivation: To examine the incompatibility between general relativity and quantum mechanics at the Planck scale by determining the computational requirements needed to challenge classical physics and test quantum-gravity theories.
AI.method: Quantify the relationship between logical qubit count and the ability to exceed classical computational limits (one operation per Planck volume-time, or 2^491 m^-3 s^-1). Analyze operational costs of computation and communication at all scales up to the observable universe.
AI.result: 500 logical qubits are sufficient to reject theories confined to laboratory settings; 1600 logical qubits are required to challenge classical physics across the entire observable universe. Current commercial quantum computer development plans are projected to surpass this 1600-qubit threshold.
AI.conclusion: The quantum-gravity standoff can be empirically tested using quantum computers with sufficient logical qubits, and current technological trajectories suggest this test may be feasible in the near future.

title: Probabilistic and approximate universal quantum purification machines
summary: We study the task of lifting arbitrary quantum states and channels to purifications and Stinespring dilations, respectively, in both the probabilistic exact and deterministic approximate settings. We formalize this task through a general framework of quantum purification machines that, given a finite number of copies or uses of a black-box input, aim to output a corresponding purification or Stinespring dilation. In the probabilistic exact setting, we show that universality is not necessary to rule out such transformations: the simple requirement that a machine purifies two inputs of different rank with non-zero probability already implies that it cannot be described by a linear positive map. This simple argument captures a fundamental obstruction of quantum theory and recovers the impossibility of universal probabilistic purification from finitely many copies. In the approximate setting, we allow for general machines that are not required, in general, to produce a pure output. Using the minimum average error as our figure of merit, we derive analytical expressions for the performance of several physically motivated strategies as well as a general upper bound on the achievable error, which is tight in a specific regime. Our analysis reveals a trade-off: strategies that produce a pure output - among which we prove the optimal to be a strategy that produces as a fixed output a maximally entangled purification of the fully depolarizing channel - perform optimally between those considered for large environment dimension, while append-environment strategies that generally produce non-pure outputs perform better at small environment dimension.

AI.tldr: The paper studies quantum state/channel purification and Stinespring dilation, showing fundamental limitations in probabilistic exact settings and analyzing performance trade-offs in approximate settings.
AI.motivation: To understand the fundamental limitations and achievable performance in lifting quantum states/channels to their purified/dilated forms, which is crucial for quantum information processing and understanding quantum theory's structure.
AI.method: Develops a framework of quantum purification machines; analyzes probabilistic exact setting showing linear positive maps cannot purify inputs of different rank; studies approximate setting using minimum average error as figure of merit, deriving analytical expressions for various strategies and general upper bounds.
AI.result: In exact setting: simple requirement to purify two different-rank inputs with non-zero probability already implies impossibility via linear positive maps. In approximate setting: trade-off between pure-output strategies (optimal at large environment dimension) and append-environment strategies (better at small environment dimension); optimal pure-output strategy uses maximally entangled purification of fully depolarizing channel.
AI.conclusion: The paper reveals fundamental obstructions in quantum theory for exact purification and establishes performance trade-offs in approximate purification, providing analytical tools and bounds for quantum purification machines.

title: Directional and correlated optical emission from a waveguide-engineered molecule with local control
summary: Radiative coupling between quantum emitters leads to a range of spectacular emission phenomena. Dicke studied the foundations of collectively enhanced and suppressed decay, commonly referred to as super- and subradiance. Collective effects can further result in directionality of the emission, thus offering a complimentary implementation of chiral quantum optics. Waveguide quantum electrodynamics (QED) allows coupling between spatially separated emitters, enabling selective driving. In this work, we control the emission direction for a pair of quantum dots embedded in a bidirectional photonic crystal waveguide offering independent electrical tuning. Notably the emitters are 13 \micro m apart, which corresponds to 26 effective wavelengths, but are nevertheless radiatively coupled. The directionality arises from a dispersive dipole-dipole interaction, which shifts the energy of the collective states, so that the emitter pair effectively forms an artificial molecule. We show that the emission direction can be switched from left- to rightwards by manipulating the relative driving phase while collectively exciting the emitters. In addition, we observe directional photon statistics under continuous driving, with, for example, single photons detected on one output port, and photon pairs on the other. With pulsed excitation, both emitters are fully inverted and correlated photon pairs are observed in time-resolved intensity correlation measurements. This work demonstrates a novel implementation of chiral quantum optics using quantum dots coupled via a non-chiral waveguide, and reports key steps for scaling up as a multi-emitter waveguide QED platform.

AI.tldr: Researchers demonstrate directional emission control in quantum dots coupled via a photonic crystal waveguide, achieving chiral quantum optics effects through dispersive dipole-dipole interactions despite large spatial separation.
AI.motivation: To implement chiral quantum optics using non-chiral waveguides by controlling emission directionality through radiative coupling between spatially separated quantum emitters, enabling scalable multi-emitter waveguide QED platforms.
AI.method: Used a pair of quantum dots embedded in a bidirectional photonic crystal waveguide with independent electrical tuning, separated by 13 μm (26 effective wavelengths). Employed dispersive dipole-dipole interactions to create collective states forming an artificial molecule, with control over relative driving phase for emission direction switching.
AI.result: Successfully demonstrated switchable emission direction (left to right) by manipulating relative driving phase, observed directional photon statistics with single photons on one port and photon pairs on the other under continuous driving, and achieved correlated photon pairs with pulsed excitation and full emitter inversion.
AI.conclusion: This work presents a novel implementation of chiral quantum optics using quantum dots coupled via non-chiral waveguides, demonstrating key capabilities for scaling up multi-emitter waveguide QED platforms through controlled radiative coupling and directional emission.

title: Strong nonlocality with more imaginarity and less entanglement
summary: Complex numbers are central to the formulation of quantum mechanics, yet their role as a genuine resource is only beginning to be understood. In this work, we demonstrate that quantum states with intrinsically complex amplitudes provide a fundamental advantage in state discrimination. We construct a set of five orthogonal three qubit pure states and show that the set is strongly nonlocal if and only if it includes imaginary components. Such a set becomes locally indistinguishable not only under local measurements but also against bipartite joint measurements. This enhanced robustness makes imaginarity a valuable resource for quantum cryptography since information encoded in these states remains secure against collaborative group attacks. Our results highlight a new operational role of complex numbers in quantum theory and establish imaginarity as a key enabler of cryptographic security. However, we reconstruct the set by replacing the only product state with a biseparable state whose shared entanglement between two parties nullifies the effect of imaginarity in exhibiting strong nonlocality. In fact, we show how entangling correlations between two distant parties can dilute the effect of imaginarity, and conversely, how imaginarity itself can mimic the role of entanglement. Nevertheless, the set spans a locally indistinguishable subspace, while its complement, in turn, produces distillable genuine entanglement. Notably, this is the smallest possible Unextendible Biseparable Basis (UBB) that resolves the open problem regarding the existence of a UBB of cardinality $d^2+d-1$ in $d^{\otimes 3}$. Our construction yields a highly powerful set, rich in resources from multiple perspectives of quantum information theory, including many-copy discrimination, unambiguous identification, entanglement creation from product state, and non-entangling perturbations.

AI.tldr: Quantum states with complex amplitudes provide fundamental advantage in state discrimination; a set of five orthogonal 3-qubit states exhibits strong nonlocality only with imaginary components, enabling cryptographic security against collaborative attacks.
AI.motivation: To understand the operational role of complex numbers (imaginarity) as a genuine resource in quantum mechanics, particularly for state discrimination and cryptographic security, and to explore the interplay between imaginarity and entanglement.
AI.method: Construct a set of five orthogonal three-qubit pure states and analyze their nonlocal properties. Investigate how imaginarity enables strong nonlocality (local indistinguishability even under bipartite joint measurements). Replace the only product state with a biseparable state to study how entanglement affects imaginarity's role. Form the smallest possible Unextendible Biseparable Basis (UBB) in d⊗3.
AI.result: The set exhibits strong nonlocality if and only if it includes imaginary components. Imaginarity provides cryptographic security against collaborative group attacks. Entanglement between two parties can dilute imaginarity's effect, while imaginarity can mimic entanglement. The constructed set is the smallest possible UBB of cardinality d²+d-1 in d⊗3, resolving an open problem. The set enables many-copy discrimination, unambiguous identification, entanglement creation from product states, and non-entangling perturbations.
AI.conclusion: Imaginarity is a fundamental quantum resource that enables strong nonlocality and cryptographic security. It exhibits complex interplay with entanglement - sometimes mimicking it, sometimes being diluted by it. The constructed UBB represents a powerful resource set with applications across multiple quantum information tasks, establishing imaginarity as a key enabler of quantum advantages.

title: Agent Choice via Quantum Flux in Living Systems
summary: A basic model is provided that places active, intentional choices by biological organisms on a solid physical footing. The model is provisionally called "Agent Choice via Quantum Flux." It brings to bear specific physics on living systems in a way that allows for intentional choices not pre-determined by physical laws, but remaining consistent with those laws. It does so by exploring a possible many-to-one relation of quantum states to agent choices, with a parallel to the relation of thermodynamic microstates to macrostates.

AI.tldr: A physics-based model called "Agent Choice via Quantum Flux" proposes that intentional choices in biological organisms emerge from quantum processes, allowing non-deterministic agency while remaining consistent with physical laws.
AI.motivation: To establish a physical foundation for active, intentional choices by biological organisms that are not predetermined by physical laws but remain consistent with them, bridging the gap between agency and physics.
AI.method: Proposes a model exploring a many-to-one relation of quantum states to agent choices, analogous to the relation between thermodynamic microstates and macrostates, using quantum flux mechanisms.
AI.result: The model provides a theoretical framework where intentional choices emerge from quantum processes, offering a physical basis for agency without violating physical laws.
AI.conclusion: The "Agent Choice via Quantum Flux" model successfully places intentional biological choices on solid physical footing by leveraging quantum indeterminacy in a manner analogous to statistical thermodynamics.

title: Dissipative Hamilton Jacobi Dynamics and the Emergence of Quantum Wave Mechanics
comment: 17 pages, 0 figures, not submitted for publishing
summary: We develop a dissipative extension of classical mechanics based on a complex, and more generally quaternionic, action principle that endows every classical system with an intrinsic environment. Decomposing the action into conservative and divergence-induced components yields two coupled Hamilton Jacobi equations describing a dynamically intertwined system environment pair. This motivates a Dual Sector or Dual Environmental Interpretation (DSI/DEI), in which the additional degrees of freedom behave as an image sector exchanging energy, information, and phase with the system. Applying a generalized Madelung transform produces a nonlinear dissipative wave equation whose symmetric equilibrium limit reduces to the Schroedinger equation, with the quantum potential and linearity emerging from balanced intersector coupling. In this framework, the wavefunction is not fundamental but encodes the interaction geometry between system and environment, providing a classical origin for interference, amplitude phase coupling, and probabilistic structure. Extending the imaginary structure to multiple independent directions yields a multienvironment generalization capable of representing measurement-like processes, nonMarkovian memory, and entanglement type correlations. The formulation unifies aspects of dual-system models, hydrodynamic approaches, and non-Hermitian dynamics within a single action-based framework, and suggests that quantum mechanics corresponds to a stable symmetric phase of a broader dissipative classical theory.

AI.tldr: A dissipative extension of classical mechanics using complex/quaternionic action principles creates intrinsic environments, leading to quantum mechanics as a symmetric equilibrium limit of a broader classical theory.
AI.motivation: To develop a classical foundation for quantum phenomena by extending classical mechanics with dissipative structures that naturally generate quantum-like behavior, providing a classical origin for interference, probability, and entanglement.
AI.method: Complex/quaternionic action principle decomposition into conservative and divergence components, generating coupled Hamilton-Jacobi equations. Generalized Madelung transform produces nonlinear dissipative wave equations, with quantum mechanics emerging as symmetric equilibrium limit.
AI.result: Quantum mechanics emerges as a stable symmetric phase of dissipative classical theory, with wavefunction encoding system-environment interaction geometry rather than being fundamental. Framework unifies dual-system models, hydrodynamic approaches, and non-Hermitian dynamics.
AI.conclusion: Quantum mechanics can be understood as a special symmetric equilibrium case of a broader dissipative classical theory, where quantum phenomena like interference and entanglement arise from balanced intersector coupling between system and intrinsic environment.

title: Higher rates for semi-device-independent randomness expansion by recycling input randomness
summary: Although quantum random number generators rely on the inherent indeterminism of quantum mechanics, ensuring that the numbers produced are secure remains a significant challenge. We introduce two semi-device-independent randomness expansion protocols in a prepare-and-measure setting, where the source and measurement devices are treated as uncharacterised and we assume trust only in testing device, which could be implemented using a photodiode. One protocol achieves expansion by recycling the input randomness, while the other uses a biased input distribution to achieve expansion in settings where recycling is not possible. The protocols are proven secure against quantum side information. Our results show that high randomness rates are achievable under experimentally realistic conditions, with expansion obtained in as few as $10^5$ to $10^6$ rounds with the recycling protocol.

AI.tldr: Semi-device-independent quantum randomness expansion protocols using prepare-and-measure setup with trusted testing device, achieving secure randomness expansion against quantum side information.
AI.motivation: Quantum random number generators face security challenges despite relying on quantum indeterminism; need for practical protocols that work with uncharacterized devices while ensuring security.
AI.method: Two semi-device-independent protocols in prepare-and-measure setting: 1) recycling input randomness for expansion, 2) using biased input distribution when recycling not possible. Both assume trust only in testing device (e.g., photodiode).
AI.result: Protocols proven secure against quantum side information; high randomness rates achievable under realistic experimental conditions; expansion obtained in 10^5 to 10^6 rounds with recycling protocol.
AI.conclusion: Practical semi-device-independent randomness expansion is feasible with minimal trusted components, enabling secure quantum random number generation in realistic experimental setups.

title: Quantum Fragmentation
summary: We introduce a systematic protocol for constructing quantum Hilbert-space-fragmented Hamiltonians, whose Krylov-sector structure, unlike in classically fragmented models, can be fully resolved only in an entangled basis. The protocol takes as input a classically fragmented model and uses a Rokhsar-Kivelson type construction to promote it to a quantum fragmented model. Notably, the procedure also works with non-fragmented inputs (such as Ising models). We explain how the Krylov sectors of the resulting quantum fragmented model may be labeled and counted in one dimension, and outline experimentally accessible verification of quantum fragmentation, assuming the ability to prepare specific initial states and perform tomography on reduced density matrices. We further analyze the entanglement structure of the entangled basis underlying quantum fragmentation, which sharply distinguishes it from both classical fragmentation and the trivial "fragmentation" of generic Hamiltonians in their eigenbasis. We also extend the construction to higher dimensions, with an explicit proof of principle example in two dimensions. We expect these results to open a new route to the systematic exploration of quantum fragmentation.

AI.tldr: Systematic protocol converts classical fragmented or non-fragmented models into quantum fragmented Hamiltonians using Rokhsar-Kivelson construction, with entangled basis revealing Krylov sectors inaccessible in classical fragmentation.
AI.motivation: To develop a systematic approach for constructing quantum Hilbert-space-fragmented Hamiltonians that go beyond classical fragmentation, where Krylov sectors can only be fully resolved in an entangled basis, enabling new exploration of quantum fragmentation phenomena.
AI.method: Uses Rokhsar-Kivelson type construction to promote classical fragmented models (or non-fragmented inputs like Ising models) to quantum fragmented models. Protocol includes labeling and counting Krylov sectors in 1D, analyzing entanglement structure of the entangled basis, and extending to higher dimensions with explicit 2D examples.
AI.result: Developed systematic protocol for constructing quantum fragmented Hamiltonians with fully resolvable Krylov sectors only in entangled basis. Provides methods for labeling/counting sectors in 1D, experimental verification protocols using specific initial states and reduced density matrix tomography, and demonstrates extension to 2D with proof-of-principle examples.
AI.conclusion: The protocol enables systematic exploration of quantum fragmentation, distinguishing it from classical fragmentation and trivial eigenbasis fragmentation through unique entanglement structure, with potential experimental verification pathways and extensions to higher dimensions.

title: One-to-one correspondence between Hierarchical Equations of Motion and Pseudomodes for Open Quantum System Dynamics
summary: We unite two of the most widely used approaches for strongly damped, non-Markovian open quantum dynamics, the Hierarchical Equations of Motion (HEOM) and the pseudomode method by proving two statements: First, every physical bath correlation function (BCF) that can be written as a sum of $N$ exponential terms can be obtained from a physical model with $N$ interacting pseudomodes which are damped in Lindblad form. Second, for every such BCF there exists a non-unitary, linear transformation which mirrors the evolution of the system-pseudomode state onto the HEOM hierarchy, and vice versa. Our proofs are constructive and we give explicit expressions for the mirror transformation as well as for the pseudomode Lindbladian corresponding to a given exponential BCF. This approach also gives insight and provides elegant derivations of the corresponding Hierarchy of stochastic Pure States (HOPS) method and its nearly-unitary version, nuHOPS. Our result opens several avenues for further optimization of non-Markovian open quantum system dynamics methods.

AI.tldr: The paper establishes a mathematical equivalence between two major methods for non-Markovian open quantum dynamics (HEOM and pseudomode method) by proving that any bath correlation function decomposable into N exponential terms can be modeled with N interacting pseudomodes, and providing explicit transformations between the two frameworks.
AI.motivation: To unify two widely used approaches for strongly damped, non-Markovian open quantum dynamics (Hierarchical Equations of Motion and pseudomode method) by establishing their mathematical equivalence and providing explicit transformations between them.
AI.method: Constructive proofs showing: 1) Any physical bath correlation function decomposable into N exponential terms can be obtained from a physical model with N interacting pseudomodes damped in Lindblad form; 2) For every such BCF, there exists a non-unitary linear transformation that mirrors system-pseudomode evolution onto the HEOM hierarchy and vice versa.
AI.result: Explicit expressions for the mirror transformation between HEOM and pseudomode frameworks, as well as for the pseudomode Lindbladian corresponding to any exponential bath correlation function. The approach also provides elegant derivations of HOPS and nuHOPS methods.
AI.conclusion: The established equivalence opens several avenues for further optimization of non-Markovian open quantum system dynamics methods by allowing cross-fertilization between HEOM and pseudomode approaches.

title: Soft-Quantum Algorithms
summary: Quantum operations on pure states can be fully represented by unitary matrices. Variational quantum circuits, also known as quantum neural networks, embed data and trainable parameters into gate-based operations and optimize the parameters via gradient descent. The high cost of training and low fidelity of current quantum devices, however, restricts much of quantum machine learning to classical simulation. For few-qubit problems with large datasets, training the matrix elements directly, as is done with weight matrices in classical neural networks, can be faster than decomposing data and parameters into gates. We propose a method that trains matrices directly while maintaining unitarity through a single regularization term added to the loss function. A second training step, circuit alignment, then recovers a gate-based architecture from the resulting soft-unitary. On a five-qubit supervised classification task with 1000 datapoints, this two-step process produces a trained variational circuit in under four minutes, compared to over two hours for direct circuit training, while achieving lower binary cross-entropy loss. In a second experiment, soft-unitaries are embedded in a hybrid quantum-classical network for a reinforcement learning cartpole task, where the hybrid agent outperforms a purely classical baseline of comparable size.

AI.tldr: Two-step method trains matrices directly with unitarity regularization, then recovers gate-based circuits, achieving faster training than direct circuit optimization while maintaining performance.
AI.motivation: Current quantum machine learning faces challenges: high training costs and low fidelity of quantum devices restrict most work to classical simulation. For few-qubit problems with large datasets, training matrix elements directly can be faster than decomposing data and parameters into gates, but maintaining unitarity is essential.
AI.method: Proposes a two-step method: 1) Train matrices directly while maintaining unitarity through a single regularization term added to the loss function, producing "soft-unitaries." 2) Circuit alignment step recovers a gate-based architecture from the resulting soft-unitary matrix.
AI.result: On a five-qubit supervised classification task with 1000 datapoints: two-step process produces trained variational circuit in under 4 minutes vs. over 2 hours for direct circuit training, achieving lower binary cross-entropy loss. In reinforcement learning cartpole task: hybrid quantum-classical network with soft-unitaries outperforms purely classical baseline of comparable size.
AI.conclusion: The proposed method enables faster training of variational quantum circuits by directly optimizing matrix elements with unitarity regularization, then recovering gate-based architectures, demonstrating practical advantages for quantum machine learning on classical simulators.

title: High-Dimensional Quantum Photonics: Roadmap
summary: The field of high-dimensional quantum photonics involves the use of multimode photonic degrees-of-freedom such as the spatial, temporal, or spectral structure of light to encode multi-level quantum states. Recent years have seen rapid progress in the development of methods to generate, manipulate, and distribute such quantum states of light and their use in a range of quantum technology applications that offer practical advantages over conventional qubit-based approaches. High-dimensional quantum states of light encoded in photonic time-bins, frequency-bins, transverse-spatial modes, waveguide paths, and temporal modes have enabled noise-robust fundamental tests of quantum mechanics, error-resilient and high-capacity quantum communication protocols, andas well as efficient approaches for quantum information processing, to name just a few examples. However, research in this field has progressed fairly independently, with little exchange across different photonic degrees-of-freedom or between experiment and theory and no comprehensive comparison between degrees-of-freedom. This roadmap aims to bridge this gap by surveying progress in each area and identifying shared challenges and opportunities that cut across two or more photonic degrees-of-freedoms. We review early work and state-of-the-art experimental techniques under development for high-dimensional quantum states encoded in single and entangled photons, as well as theoretical tools for their measurement and certification. We outline the main outstanding challenges for theory and each experimental degree-of-freedom, identifying promising future directions of research that may enable these to be overcome. We end by discussing interconnections and shared challenges centered around their distribution, measurement, and manipulation, with a view towards their integration into next-generation quantum technology platforms and applications.

AI.tldr: This roadmap paper surveys high-dimensional quantum photonics across different photonic degrees-of-freedom, identifies shared challenges, and outlines future research directions for integration into quantum technology platforms.
AI.motivation: The field of high-dimensional quantum photonics has progressed independently across different photonic degrees-of-freedom with little exchange between experiment and theory, lacking comprehensive comparisons. This roadmap aims to bridge these gaps by surveying progress, identifying shared challenges, and fostering integration.
AI.method: The paper employs a comprehensive survey approach, reviewing early work and state-of-the-art experimental techniques for high-dimensional quantum states encoded in single and entangled photons across various degrees-of-freedom (time-bins, frequency-bins, spatial modes, waveguide paths, temporal modes). It also examines theoretical tools for measurement and certification, identifies outstanding challenges for each degree-of-freedom, and discusses interconnections between different approaches.
AI.result: The roadmap provides a unified perspective on high-dimensional quantum photonics, highlighting progress in noise-robust quantum mechanics tests, error-resilient quantum communication, high-capacity protocols, and efficient quantum information processing. It identifies shared challenges in distribution, measurement, and manipulation across different photonic degrees-of-freedom.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes by outlining promising future research directions to overcome existing challenges and emphasizes the need for integration of different photonic degrees-of-freedom into next-generation quantum technology platforms and applications, fostering cross-disciplinary collaboration in the field.

title: Discrete-variable assisted error correction of continuous-variable quantum information
summary: Robust continuous-variable (CV) quantum information processing requires correcting realistic errors in bosonic systems, but all existing schemes rely on auxiliary Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) states which the preparation and operation are demanding in many platforms. In this work, we propose a novel CV quantum error correction (QEC) scheme that utilizes a broadly accessible resource: discrete-variable (DV) ancilla. Our scheme extracts information about CV displacement to the DV ancilla, measuring that allows counteracting the unwanted displacement error. We show that a simple single-qubit ancilla can already suppress CV infidelity by more than 20%. By concatenating with DV QEC codes, our scheme is robust against the physical errors in hybrid CV-DV systems, and yields a new class of oscillator-in-oscillator code that does not involve GKP states. Our work facilitates the implementation of CV QEC on realistic platforms.

AI.tldr: A novel CV quantum error correction scheme using discrete-variable ancilla instead of demanding GKP states, achieving >20% infidelity suppression with single-qubit ancilla and enabling robust hybrid CV-DV systems.
AI.motivation: Robust CV quantum information processing requires error correction, but existing schemes rely on demanding Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) states that are difficult to prepare and operate in many platforms.
AI.method: Proposes a CV QEC scheme using discrete-variable ancilla to extract information about CV displacement errors. The scheme measures displacement errors via DV ancilla and counteracts them. Can be concatenated with DV QEC codes for robustness against physical errors in hybrid systems.
AI.result: Shows that a simple single-qubit ancilla can suppress CV infidelity by more than 20%. The scheme creates a new class of oscillator-in-oscillator codes without GKP states and is robust against physical errors in hybrid CV-DV systems.
AI.conclusion: This work facilitates the implementation of CV quantum error correction on realistic platforms by eliminating the need for demanding GKP states and instead utilizing broadly accessible discrete-variable ancilla resources.

title: Coherent feedback $H^\infty$ control of quantum linear systems
summary: The purpose of this paper is to investigate the coherent feedback $H^\infty$ control problem for linear quantum systems. A key contribution is a simplified design methodology that guarantees closed-loop stability and a prescribed level of disturbance attenuation. It is shown that for general linear quantum systems, a physically realizable quantum controller can be obtained by solving at most four Lyapunov equations. In the passive case, a necessary and sufficient condition is provided in terms of two uncoupled pairs of Lyapunov equations. These results represent a significant simplification over the standard approach, which requires solving two coupled algebraic Riccati equations. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through two typical quantum optical devices: an empty optical cavity and a degenerate parametric amplifier. These results provide a computationally efficient procedure for the robust and optimal control of quantum optical and optomechanical systems.

AI.tldr: Simplified coherent feedback H∞ control for linear quantum systems using Lyapunov equations instead of coupled Riccati equations.
AI.motivation: To develop a computationally efficient design methodology for coherent feedback H∞ control of linear quantum systems that guarantees stability and disturbance attenuation.
AI.method: Proposes solving at most four Lyapunov equations for general linear quantum systems, and two uncoupled pairs of Lyapunov equations for passive systems, instead of the standard approach requiring two coupled algebraic Riccati equations.
AI.result: Demonstrates effectiveness through quantum optical devices (empty optical cavity and degenerate parametric amplifier), showing physically realizable quantum controllers can be obtained with simplified computation.
AI.conclusion: Provides a computationally efficient procedure for robust and optimal control of quantum optical and optomechanical systems, representing significant simplification over standard approaches.

title: Database Reordering for Compact Grover Oracles with ESOP Minimization
summary:
Grover's algorithm searches for data satisfying a desired condition in an unstructured database. This algorithm can search a space of size $N$ in $\sqrt{N}$ queries, thereby achieving a quadratic speedup. However, within the Grover oracle circuit that is repeatedly applied, the quantum state preparation circuit -- which embeds database information into quantum states -- suffers from a large gate count and circuit depth. To address this problem, we propose reducing the quantum state preparation circuit by reordering the database. Specifically, we consider a Quantum Read-Only Memory (QROM), where data are assigned to addresses, and assume that the address assignment of data can be freely permuted. By applying Exclusive Sum-of-Products (ESOP) minimization to the resulting truth table, we reduce the quantum circuit. Although the resulting circuit logic differs from the original, the state preparation remains correct in the sense that every desired datum is encoded at some address. Furthermore, we propose a proxy metric that estimates circuit size without compilation, and combine it with simulated annealing to efficiently find a near-optimal data ordering.
  In our experiments, an exhaustive search over all orderings for databases of size $N=8$ reveals that circuit size varies by up to approximately a factor of two depending on the ordering, demonstrating the utility of reordering. Compared with applying ESOP minimization without reordering, simulated annealing reduces the circuit size by approximately 30\% and yields circuits close to optimal. For $N=64$ and $128$, simulated annealing is shown to discover smaller circuits compared with random search.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes reordering database entries in Quantum Read-Only Memory (QROM) to reduce quantum state preparation circuit complexity in Grover's algorithm, using ESOP minimization and simulated annealing to find near-optimal orderings.
AI.motivation: The quantum state preparation circuit in Grover's algorithm suffers from large gate count and circuit depth when embedding database information into quantum states, creating a bottleneck for practical implementation.
AI.method: Proposes reordering database entries in QROM where address assignment can be freely permuted, then applies ESOP minimization to the resulting truth table to reduce quantum circuit complexity. Uses a proxy metric to estimate circuit size without compilation and combines it with simulated annealing to efficiently find near-optimal data orderings.
AI.result: For N=8 databases, circuit size varies by up to ~2x depending on ordering. Simulated annealing reduces circuit size by ~30% compared to ESOP minimization without reordering, yielding circuits close to optimal. For N=64 and 128, simulated annealing discovers smaller circuits than random search.
AI.conclusion: Database reordering combined with ESOP minimization and simulated annealing optimization effectively reduces quantum state preparation circuit complexity in Grover's algorithm, making the algorithm more practical for quantum computing applications.

title: Deterministic linear-optical computing with symmetry-based qubits
summary: A particular type of linear optical multiport, the Grover four-port, has previously been shown to couple the spatial symmetry of a photon to its direction of travel. It is shown here that use of a nonstandard choice of qubit, based on symmetry, allows Grover four ports to act as compact, low-resource deterministic linear optical controlledNOTgates, with no post-selection or ancilla measurements required. This approach allows programmable devices, made from Grover multiports in combination with other standard optical components, that can implement multiple different one-, two-, and three-qubit gates, including the Fredkin and Toffoli gates.

AI.tldr: Grover four-ports enable deterministic linear optical CNOT gates using symmetry-based qubits, without post-selection or ancilla measurements, allowing programmable multi-qubit gate implementation.
AI.motivation: To develop compact, low-resource deterministic linear optical quantum gates that avoid the need for post-selection or ancilla measurements, which are resource-intensive in conventional linear optical quantum computing approaches.
AI.method: Utilizes Grover four-ports with symmetry-based qubit encoding, where photon spatial symmetry is coupled to direction of travel. Combines Grover multiports with standard optical components to create programmable devices.
AI.result: Demonstrates deterministic linear optical CNOT gates, and programmable devices capable of implementing various one-, two-, and three-qubit gates including Fredkin and Toffoli gates.
AI.conclusion: Symmetry-based qubit encoding with Grover four-ports provides a resource-efficient approach to deterministic linear optical quantum computing, enabling programmable multi-qubit gate implementation without post-selection requirements.

title: Quantifying magic via quantum $(α,β)$ Jensen-Shannon divergence
summary: Magic states play an important role in fault-tolerant quantum computation, and so the quantification of magic for quantum states is of great significance. In this work, we propose two new magic quantifiers by introducing two versions of quantum $(α,β)$ Jensen-Shannon divergence based on the quantum $(α,β)$ entropy and the quantum $(α,β)$-relative entropy, respectively. We derive many desirable properties for our magic quantifiers, and find that they are efficiently computable in low-dimensional Hilbert spaces. We also show that the initial nonstabilizerness in the input state can boost the magic generating power for our magic quantifiers with appropriate parameter ranges for a certain class of quantum gates. Our magic quantifiers may provide new tools for addressing some specific problems in magic resource theory.

AI.tldr: Two new magic quantifiers based on quantum (α,β) Jensen-Shannon divergence derived from quantum (α,β) entropy and relative entropy, with desirable properties, efficient computability in low dimensions, and demonstration of how initial nonstabilizerness can boost magic generation.
AI.motivation: Magic states are crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, necessitating effective quantification methods for quantum magic. Existing approaches may have limitations, prompting development of new quantifiers with better theoretical properties and practical utility.
AI.method: Introduce two versions of quantum (α,β) Jensen-Shannon divergence based on quantum (α,β) entropy and quantum (α,β)-relative entropy to create new magic quantifiers. Derive mathematical properties, analyze computational efficiency, and investigate how initial nonstabilizerness affects magic generation with specific quantum gates.
AI.result: The proposed magic quantifiers exhibit many desirable properties and are efficiently computable in low-dimensional Hilbert spaces. The study shows that initial nonstabilizerness in input states can enhance magic generating power for appropriate parameter ranges with certain quantum gates.
AI.conclusion: The new magic quantifiers provide valuable tools for magic resource theory, offering improved quantification methods with favorable mathematical properties and practical computational advantages for addressing specific problems in quantum computation.

title: Enhanced Precision in Entangled Quantum Clocks with Phase Estimation Algorithm
summary: We present an enhanced entangled quantum clock protocol that incorporates a quantum phase estimation algorithm to directly estimate proper-time differences as an unknown phase. By employing highly entangled multi-clock states, the achievable uncertainty scales inversely with the total number of quantum clocks, surpassing the standard projection-noise limit. This approach extends the original EQC framework and provides a systematic method for high-precision relativistic time comparison.

AI.tldr: Enhanced entangled quantum clock protocol uses quantum phase estimation with multi-clock entanglement to achieve uncertainty scaling inversely with total clock number, surpassing standard limits for high-precision relativistic time comparison.
AI.motivation: To overcome the standard projection-noise limit in quantum clock protocols and enable high-precision relativistic time comparison by directly estimating proper-time differences as quantum phases.
AI.method: Incorporates quantum phase estimation algorithm into entangled quantum clock protocol, using highly entangled multi-clock states to directly estimate proper-time differences as unknown phases.
AI.result: Achievable uncertainty scales inversely with the total number of quantum clocks, surpassing the standard projection-noise limit, extending the original EQC framework.
AI.conclusion: The enhanced protocol provides a systematic method for high-precision relativistic time comparison using quantum entanglement and phase estimation techniques.

title: Coherence and entanglement dynamics in Shor's algorithm
summary: Shor's algorithm outperforms its classical counterpart in efficient prime factorization. We explore the coherence and entanglement dynamics of the evolved states within Shor's algorithm, showing that the coherence in each step relies on the dimension of register or the order, and discuss the relations between geometric coherence and geometric entanglement. We investigate how unitary operators induce variations in coherence and entanglement, and analyze the variations of coherence and entanglement within the entire algorithm, demonstrating that the overall effect of Shor's algorithm tends to deplete coherence and produce entanglement. Our research not only deepens the understanding of this algorithm but also provides methodological references for studying resource dynamics in other quantum algorithms.

AI.tldr: Analysis of coherence and entanglement dynamics in Shor's algorithm, showing algorithm depletes coherence and produces entanglement, with coherence depending on register dimension or order.
AI.motivation: To understand the quantum resource dynamics (coherence and entanglement) within Shor's algorithm, which outperforms classical factorization, and provide methodological references for studying other quantum algorithms.
AI.method: Explore coherence and entanglement dynamics of evolved states in Shor's algorithm, analyze how unitary operators induce variations in these resources, and examine relations between geometric coherence and geometric entanglement.
AI.result: Coherence in each step depends on register dimension or order; overall effect of Shor's algorithm tends to deplete coherence and produce entanglement; unitary operators induce variations in coherence and entanglement.
AI.conclusion: Research deepens understanding of Shor's algorithm and provides methodological framework for studying resource dynamics in other quantum algorithms, revealing fundamental quantum resource trade-offs in quantum computation.

title: Quantum target ranging with Hetero-Homodyne detection
summary: Quantum target ranging, which estimates a target position using entangled photon pairs, is known to offer an error-probability advantage over classical ranging strategies. Yet, realizing this advantage in practice remains challenging, as an existing receiver design relies on collective measurements and requires an impractically large number of quantum memories and linear passive components. In this work, we propose the hetero-homodyne receiver, a practically implementable architecture that achieves quantum advantage in target ranging using only local measurements. The receiver requires only one heterodyne setup, a single homodyne setup, and a delay line, making the implementation scalable and experimentally feasible. Our results establish a realistic framework for demonstrating quantum advantage in target ranging and contribute toward practical quantum radar systems.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a practical hetero-homodyne receiver architecture for quantum target ranging that achieves quantum advantage using only local measurements, overcoming implementation challenges of previous designs.
AI.motivation: Existing quantum ranging receivers require impractical collective measurements with many quantum memories and passive components, making experimental realization challenging despite theoretical quantum advantage.
AI.method: Proposed hetero-homodyne receiver architecture using only one heterodyne setup, a single homodyne setup, and a delay line, enabling local measurements without collective operations.
AI.result: The receiver achieves quantum advantage in target ranging while being scalable and experimentally feasible, requiring minimal components compared to previous designs.
AI.conclusion: The work establishes a realistic framework for demonstrating quantum advantage in target ranging and contributes toward practical quantum radar systems.

title: Environment-Assisted Decoherence Suppression of Optical Non-Gaussian States
summary: Optical loss is a common bottleneck in photonic quantum information processing, undermining the quantum advantage over classical approaches. Although several countermeasures, such as quantum distillation and error correction, have been proposed, they typically require experimentally demanding non-Gaussian operations. Here, we demonstrate a Gaussian-only scheme that suppresses loss-induced decoherence for general, unknown optical quantum states. By injecting a squeezed vacuum state into an environment of the loss channel and performing feedforward based on environmental monitoring, the scheme effectively suppresses loss-induced noise. Our programmable loop-based optical circuit allows us to implement the scheme for several types of loss-sensitive non-Gaussian states under various loss conditions for up to five steps, and directly compare the results with the unsuppressed case. Our results show that the scheme consistently mitigates state degradation, preserving higher fidelity and Wigner negativity than without suppression. This approach can be applied to mitigating a broad class of errors in optical systems and extending quantum memory lifetimes. Moreover, it is compatible with other loss-suppression techniques and extendable to physical platforms beyond optics, offering a promising route toward reducing the overhead required for fault-tolerant quantum information processing.

AI.tldr: A Gaussian-only scheme suppresses loss-induced decoherence in optical quantum systems using squeezed vacuum injection and environmental monitoring feedforward, preserving quantum state fidelity without requiring non-Gaussian operations.
AI.motivation: Optical loss undermines quantum advantage in photonic quantum information processing. Existing countermeasures like quantum distillation and error correction typically require experimentally demanding non-Gaussian operations, creating a need for simpler approaches.
AI.method: A Gaussian-only scheme that injects squeezed vacuum into the loss channel environment and performs feedforward based on environmental monitoring. Implemented using a programmable loop-based optical circuit for various loss-sensitive non-Gaussian states under different loss conditions for up to five steps.
AI.result: The scheme consistently mitigates state degradation, preserving higher fidelity and Wigner negativity compared to unsuppressed cases. It effectively suppresses loss-induced noise for general, unknown optical quantum states.
AI.conclusion: This approach can mitigate broad classes of errors in optical systems, extend quantum memory lifetimes, is compatible with other loss-suppression techniques, and is extendable to physical platforms beyond optics, offering a promising route toward reducing overhead for fault-tolerant quantum information processing.

title: Perturbative hydrogenic Lamb shifts and radiative decay rates -- an so(4,2)-based algebraic approach
summary: It is shown that algebraic techniques based on the Lie algebra so(4,2) provide efficient tools for evaluating Lamb shifts and radiative decay rates for hydrogenic energy eigenstates as they systematically exploit the intrinsic symmetry of the hydrogenic Hamiltonian. As a main result in lowest order perturbation theory with respect to the fine-structure constant integral representations are derived for the complex-valued energy shifts of hydrogen-like ions from which Lamb shifts and radiative decay rates can be evaluated in a unified way, thus generalizing a recently discussed algebraic approach of Maclay. In order to exemplify the usefulness of this algebraic approach numerical results are presented for Lamb shifts and radiative decay rates which transcend the dipole approximation and contain the dipole approximation as a limiting case.

AI.tldr: Algebraic techniques using so(4,2) Lie algebra provide efficient tools for evaluating Lamb shifts and radiative decay rates in hydrogenic systems by exploiting intrinsic symmetry.
AI.motivation: To develop systematic algebraic techniques that exploit the intrinsic symmetry of the hydrogenic Hamiltonian for more efficient evaluation of Lamb shifts and radiative decay rates, generalizing Maclay's approach.
AI.method: Using algebraic techniques based on the Lie algebra so(4,2) in lowest order perturbation theory with respect to the fine-structure constant to derive integral representations for complex-valued energy shifts of hydrogen-like ions.
AI.result: Derived integral representations for complex-valued energy shifts from which Lamb shifts and radiative decay rates can be evaluated in a unified way, with numerical results presented that transcend the dipole approximation while containing it as a limiting case.
AI.conclusion: The so(4,2) algebraic approach provides efficient, systematic tools for evaluating Lamb shifts and radiative decay rates in hydrogenic systems, offering a unified framework that generalizes previous work and extends beyond dipole approximation.

title: A hardware efficient quantum residual neural network without post-selection
summary: We propose a hardware efficient quantum residual neural network which implements residual connections through a deterministic linear combination of identity and variational unitaries, enabling fully differentiable training. In contrast to the previous implementation of residual connections, our architecture avoids post-selection while preserving residual learning. Furthermore, we establish trainability of our model, mitigating barren plateaus which are considered as a major limitation of variational quantum learning models. In order to show the working of our model, we report its application to image classification tasks by training it for MNIST, CIFAR, and SARFish datasets, achieving accuracies of 99% and 80% for binary and multi-class classifications, respectively. These accuracies are comparable to previously achieved from the standard variational models, however our model requires 10x fewer gates making it better suited for resource constraint near-term quantum processors. In addition to high accuracies, the proposed architecture also demonstrates adversarial robustness which is another desirable parameter for quantum machine learning models. Overall our architecture offers a new pathway for developing accurate, robust, trainable and hardware efficient quantum machine learning models.

AI.tldr: Hardware-efficient quantum residual neural network with deterministic linear combination of identity and variational unitaries enables fully differentiable training without post-selection, mitigates barren plateaus, achieves high accuracy with 10x fewer gates, and demonstrates adversarial robustness.
AI.motivation: To develop quantum machine learning models that are hardware-efficient, trainable, and robust while overcoming limitations of existing variational quantum models like barren plateaus and resource-intensive implementations.
AI.method: Proposes a quantum residual neural network architecture that implements residual connections through deterministic linear combination of identity and variational unitaries, enabling fully differentiable training without post-selection. The model mitigates barren plateaus through established trainability guarantees.
AI.result: Achieves 99% accuracy for binary classification and 80% for multi-class classification on MNIST, CIFAR, and SARFish datasets, comparable to standard variational models but with 10x fewer gates. Demonstrates adversarial robustness.
AI.conclusion: The proposed architecture provides a new pathway for developing accurate, robust, trainable, and hardware-efficient quantum machine learning models suitable for resource-constrained near-term quantum processors.

title: Emergence of Non-Markovian Classical-Quantum Dynamics from Decoherence
summary: The quantum nature of gravity remains experimentally unverified, despite recent proposals to probe it using tabletop experiments such as gravity-mediated entanglement schemes. In parallel, consistent formulations of classical--quantum dynamics have been developed as alternative descriptions of gravity, in which quantum matter interacts with a classical mediator assumed to be fundamentally classical. In this work, we show that classical--quantum dynamics arise generically as an effective description of fully quantum systems under decoherence, providing a bridge between fully quantum and classical--quantum dynamics. We derive the reduced dynamics, which are generically non-Markovian, using an explicit hidden model in which the mediator is coupled to unobserved environmental degrees of freedom. We identify a concrete criterion for when a classical--quantum interpretation is valid: the semi-Wigner operator associated with the mediator sector must remain positive semidefinite, which can be expressed as a positivity condition on nonlocal kernels governing the evolution. In the short-memory limit, the reduced evolution reproduces Markovian classical--quantum dynamics of Oppenheim and collaborators. Our results imply that a classical mediator can arise effectively from decohered quantum dynamics, so that experimental agreement with classical-quantum models does not uniquely determine whether the mediator is fundamentally classical.

AI.tldr: Classical-quantum dynamics emerge as effective descriptions of fully quantum systems under decoherence, bridging quantum and classical-quantum frameworks, with implications for interpreting gravity experiments.
AI.motivation: To address the experimental verification of quantum gravity and reconcile proposals for tabletop gravity experiments with alternative classical-quantum formulations, by showing how classical-quantum dynamics can arise from fully quantum systems under decoherence.
AI.method: Derived reduced dynamics using an explicit hidden model where the mediator couples to unobserved environmental degrees of freedom, obtaining generically non-Markovian evolution. Identified a positivity criterion for classical-quantum interpretation validity based on semi-Wigner operator positivity.
AI.result: Classical-quantum dynamics emerge generically as effective descriptions of decohered quantum systems. In the short-memory limit, the reduced evolution reproduces Markovian classical-quantum dynamics of Oppenheim et al. The semi-Wigner operator positivity condition provides a concrete criterion for classical-quantum interpretation validity.
AI.conclusion: Classical mediators can arise effectively from decohered quantum dynamics, meaning experimental agreement with classical-quantum models does not uniquely determine whether the mediator is fundamentally classical, with significant implications for interpreting gravity experiments.

title: Quantum Relative-alpha-Entropies: A Structural and Geometric Perspective
summary: Most quantum divergences derive their structure from classical f-divergences or Renyi-type constructions, a dependence that obscures several quantum geometric effects. We introduce a quantum relative-alpha-entropy that extends Umegaki's relative entropy while falling outside the f-divergence class. The proposed divergence exhibits a nonlinear convexity property, which yields a generalized convexity result for the Petz-Renyi divergence for alpha greater than one, complementing the known convexity for alpha less than one. It is additive under tensor products, invariant under unitary transformations, and depends only on the relative geometry of quantum states rather than their absolute magnitudes. Using Nussbaum-Szkola-type distributions, we also establish an exact correspondence of this divergence with classical relative-alpha-entropy. This reveals relative-alpha-entropy as a fundamentally geometric notion of quantum distinguishability not captured by existing divergence frameworks.

AI.tldr: Introduces quantum relative-alpha-entropy that extends Umegaki's relative entropy but lies outside f-divergence class, revealing geometric quantum distinguishability not captured by existing frameworks.
